boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Aquia Creek record (May 29-June 1, 1861) in Blockade of the Chesapeake Bay [May-June 1861]. The May reconnaissances of the battery and the later Potomac operations are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads '3 gunboats [US]; battery garrison [CS]'; the live field reads zero. Ruggles reports two small steamers on the evening of the 29th, three war steamers on the 31st, and on June 1 first a report of five steamers with two transports and then four armed steamers; he took some seven hundred men toward the battery on the 29th, with five hundred more at the camp, and four companies of infantry, one of cavalry and the Walker Legion on the 31st. Ward reports the Freeborn supported by the Anacostia and Resolute on May 31 and the Pawnee joining him for June 1.
claims.rationale: Vessel counts and supporting-force figures, not the battery garrison. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Ward says he expended all ammunition suitable for distant firing on May 31 and on June 1 went to Washington to repair damages and refill his exhausted magazines, having fired upward of 300 shots and shells with 1,700 pounds of powder over the several cannonades. Ruggles asked for heavy guns, a thousand volunteers and twenty thousand musket-rifle caps, and relays that the enemy threw 597 shots and shells on June 1 against 75 from the battery.
claims.rationale: Supply statements from the two commanders; relayed shot counts are not measured expenditure returns.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel Daniel Ruggles and Commander James H. Ward (navy); the live page gives Ruggles as Brigadier General, and Ruggles signs as colonel of the Provisional Army. Ruggles says the batteries were commanded by Captain Lynch and other naval officers, and his supporting force by Colonel Bate until he arrived about midday on June 1. Ward commanded the flotilla and says he was its only Regular Navy officer, the others being acting officers from civil life.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; the battery commander is not a listed commander. No automatic sole credit; the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive; NPS calls the bombardment inconclusive and says the batteries were later withdrawn. Ward says he silenced the three terminus batteries on May 31 and on June 1 found the heights abandoned and the shore fire feeble before discontinuing. Ruggles says the steamers hauled off on May 31, supposedly partly disabled, and that on June 1 no material damage was done to the batteries and the enemy hauled off to the Maryland shore.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

open_questions: Lynch's June 2 and June 6 reports, Rowan's June 2 report, Bate's and Cluskey's letters and the May reconnaissance reports remain unselected.
The Army compilation prints Ruggles's first report as 'fired some fourteen shot and shell'; the Navy reprint reads 'with twelve shot and shell'. The difference is recorded, not resolved.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Ruggles's May 30-June 4, 1861 reports (Army Official Records Series I, Volume II) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. Ward's May 31 and June 1 reports (Navy Official Records Series I, Volume 4) are one family of interested Union accounts. The Army and Navy Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and reprints of a report in the other compilation are copies. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner history narrates this engagement; Nicolay's The Outbreak of Rebellion mentions Great Bethel only in passing.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
